source.version: Published journal version of record: Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization 242 (2026), 107414; DOI 10.1016/j.jebo.2026.107414. PDF p. 1: received 21 May 2025, revised 31 October 2025, accepted 1 January 2026, available online 15 January 2026.
source.supplement_used: Appendices A-D within the main PDF, pp. 16-21. Separate Supplementary Material linked in Appendix E is not on file and was not used.

studies.label: Wave 1 lab experiment (HI vs HAT vs HHT), picture-idea tasks 2 and 3
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Robust standard errors clustered by experimental session (PDF pp. 8, 13-14, 18, 20). clusters_per_arm records treatment-specific sessions from Table D.2 (PDF p. 19), not confirmed randomized clusters. The allocation protocol does not establish individual versus session randomization, and the random-effects level is not explicit. Resolve these points before pooling.

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 2, Section 1; PDF p. 19, Table D.2 (columns Training, HAT, HI, HHT); exclusions: PDF p. 17, Appendix B.2
counts_source.quote: In the ﬁrst wave, 246 participants were recruited and randomly assigned to one of three between-subject treatments. ... No. subjects 56 61 63 122 No. sessions 2 2 2 5

arms.name: HI (Control)
arms.description: Human individual: treated picture-idea tasks alone without ChatGPT (PDF p. 4). All arms first received the same brief ChatGPT familiarization.

arms.name: HAT
arms.description: Human-AI team: individual participant may chat freely with ChatGPT 3.5 through Poe.com while producing picture ideas (PDF pp. 4, 6).

arms.name: HHT
arms.description: Human-human team: anonymous pairs, randomly re-matched for each treated task, converse by text and submit a shared idea (PDF p. 4).

studies.task: Nankai University students describe a creative picture in fewer than 100 Chinese characters within a 12-minute soft time limit for each of two counterbalanced themes; experimenters later generate images from the descriptions (PDF pp. 5-6).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT 3.5 accessed through poe.com
ai_tool.locator: PDF pp. 4, 6, Sections 2.1 and 2.3. First-wave deployment was May-June 2023; model release year is not stated. DALL-E 3 via ChatGPT-4o was used by experimenters to render outputs, not supplied to participants (PDF p. 17).

preregistration.where: AsPredicted.org; PDF p. 6, Section 2.3. Registration and deviations are in Supplementary Section 1, not on file.

studies.shared_sample: Earlier working paper Zhu and Zou (2023), The role of generative AI in human creative processes: experimental evidence, SSRN 4676053, used the same first-wave participants with an earlier evaluation panel (PDF p. 2, footnote 2; PDF p. 22). The citation record also identifies SSRN 5196748 as a version; its overlap is not separately established in this PDF.

estimates.outcome: Image-text creativity grade; Table 3 column 2
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Mean creativity grade from 30 student evaluators per theme, using a 1-10 scale to one decimal place. Evaluators saw the submitted description and its experimenter-generated DALL-E 3 image. Theme order and evaluation-format order were counterbalanced. Image-text grades are the paper’s primary measure, but preregistered-primary status is unverified.

stats.difference_is: Adjusted HAT minus HI effect, rounded as printed in Section 3.2; same estimate as regression.coef.

regression.model: Random-effects grade model with theme, task order and pre-treatment major, belief that AI replaces humans in creativity, and prior generative-AI use; HHT ideas expanded to individual-idea rows.

paper_effect.standardizer: Regression coefficient divided by the SD of the outcome variable (Appendix C, PDF p. 18). The numeric denominator and a participant-level standardizer are not printed; do not relabel as Cohen d.

sources.quote: We implement by taking the regression coeﬃcient and standard error from the regression equations and dividing both by the standard deviation of the outcome variable.

estimates.notes: Uncertainty is session-clustered. Because the randomized unit and random-effects level are not established, se_basis is conservatively coded output for these idea-level results; this does not assert that within-session dependence was ignored. Establish the allocation protocol before treating precision as participant- or randomized-cluster-level. n_units is the printed row count for the whole fitted model, including the nonrandom Training cohort where present, not people or the sum for this pairwise contrast. Model variants are not independent samples.  Table 2 SD aggregation is unresolved: the table says grades average evaluators but does not establish whether SDs describe ratings, idea means or participant means. sd_level is null. Submission counts are quoted, not converted to people or summed. Main specification emphasized in the introduction and Section 3.2. Prefer this over alternative specifications of the same sample/outcome. Figure 1 confidence bars are unlabeled; no endpoints were read from the plot.

open_items: Assignment unit: first-wave randomization is explicit, but individual versus session allocation is not established. Obtain the supplementary protocol before pooling or assigning definitive randomization-level se_basis (PDF pp. 2, 6, 19). Session counts do not prove session randomization.

Analyzed-person counts: Appendix B.2 excludes one HAT participant from grade analyses and describes image/evaluator missingness, but exact post-exclusion first-wave total and outcome-specific people counts are not printed. Counts are not derived from exclusions, submissions or model rows (PDF pp. 8, 17).

Table 2 SD level: confirm whether SDs describe individual ratings, idea means, participant means or another aggregation. No participant-level standardizer is established. The outcome-SD denominator behind the reported standardized regression effect is also not printed (PDF pp. 8, 18).

DAT availability: confirm whether ChatGPT was removed during both post-task word-generation tests before coding with_ai or after_ai. Exact coefficients, uncertainty and analyzed-person counts are missing (PDF pp. 4, 11-12, 16-18).

Table 5 underlying image-text versus text-only grade, within-arm/theme aggregation, counts and uncertainty are unspecified. These are performance-inequality indices, not content diversity (PDF p. 10).

Preregistration and supplement: inspect Supplementary Section 1 for primary outcome and deviations, and Tables S1-S7 for additional full-sample estimates. Only the published paper primary outcome is established (PDF pp. 6, 8, 21).
AI model release year is not stated. Deployment date is documented but is not substituted for release year.

Direct HAT-versus-HHT uncertainty is printed only as the image-text comparison p-value. Other descriptive contrasts lack direct tests. Figure 1 interval endpoints are unlabeled and were not transcribed.
notes: Extraction B completed 2026-10-10. The complete markdown conversion was read in six contiguous chunks, including appendices and references. PDF tables, figures and appendices were inventoried before methods. Every cited page was extracted with pymupdf; table text was cross-checked with find_tables text strategies and clipped rows. Inventory retained: Table 2 raw/standardized human-arm grades; all noninteracted Table 3 HAT specifications; Section 3.2 rounded raw/standardized effects and HAT-HHT p-value; Table 5 CV/Gini arm levels; Table 7 baselines without mediators; Table 8 output-based rating-format effects; Table D.3 noninteraction models; Tables D.4-D.5 human-arm levels by theme. Alternatives share the same first-wave sample. Prefer s1_image_text_hat_vs_hi_main: Section 3.2 interprets Table 3 column (2), and Section 2.2 names image-text grades as primary. Preregistered-primary status is unverified. Comparisons are between assigned arms, so within_person is null despite repeated tasks and randomized theme order. No differences, SDs, sample totals, effects or confidence endpoints were calculated. Printed numeric precision and signed zero are preserved. Resolve randomization and SD details before standardization or pooling.
